title: Identification of YES1 Inhibitors From Approved Drugs Using a Multimodal Deep Learning Framework.
authors: Kawabata T, Takeda T, Tanaka Y et al.
abstract: While anti-human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) drugs, including trastuzumab improve the prognosis of patients with HER2-positive cancers, acquired resistance by cancer cells remains a significant clinical challenge. We had previously reported that YES1 is overexpressed in trastuzumab-resistant breast and lung cancer cells, and that its inhibition restores trastuzumab sensitivity. However, no approved drug specifically targets YES1. In this study, as a drug repositioning approach aimed at rapid clinical application, we constructed a machine learning model capable of learning the interactions between compounds and target proteins and conducted a screening of approved drugs. The strategy identified chlorpromazine and raloxifene as hit compounds. In vitro validation demonstrated that they effectively inhibited YES1 activation at 15 μM after 48 h. The findings suggested that the identified approved drugs might represent promising therapeutic options for overcoming anti-HER2 drug resistance.

title: Intracranial activity of amivantamab combined with carboplatin and pemetrexed in epidermal growth factor receptor exon 20 insertion-positive non-small cell lung cancer with brain metastases: a report of three cases.
authors: Fujiwara Y, Tamiya Y, Yamaguchi T et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 20 insertion (Ex20ins) mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) are largely insensitive to conventional EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) because of steric hindrance in the TKI-binding pocket. Amivantamab, an EGFR-MET bispecific antibody, has been approved for use in combination with chemotherapy as the first-line treatment for EGFR Ex20ins NSCLC. However, intracranial activity remains unknown because monoclonal antibodies are generally thought to have limited central nervous system (CNS) penetration.
CASE DESCRIPTION: We report three patients with advanced NSCLC with EGFR Ex20ins and with asymptomatic brain metastases who were treated with carboplatin, pemetrexed, and amivantamab (PAPILLON regimen). Case 1 was a 48-year-old woman with ≥10 asymptomatic brain metastases that developed during prior treatment with carboplatin, pemetrexed, and an investigational TKI targeting their EGFR ex20ins mutations; she achieved intracranial and extracranial partial responses. Case 2 was a 67-year-old man with postoperative recurrence and new brain metastases arising during another investigational EGFR-TKI monotherapy; he achieved a complete intracranial response. Case 3 was a 35-year-old man with previously untreated advanced lung adenocarcinoma and multiple asymptomatic brain metastases, which demonstrated intracranial and extracranial partial responses within two months.
CONCLUSIONS: These three cases provide clinical evidence that carboplatin, pemetrexed, and amivantamab may exert clinically meaningful intracranial antitumor activity in patients with EGFR Ex20ins NSCLC harboring small, asymptomatic brain metastases. Amivantamab, a bispecific antibody, combined with carboplatin and pemetrexed may exert clinically meaningful intracranial antitumor activity.

title: Prolonged survival in a 57-year-old female with RB1-wildtype transformed small-cell lung cancer treated with immunochemotherapy and antiangiogenic combined therapy: a case report.
authors: Kang L, Zhao L, Chen X et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transformed small-cell lung cancer (T-SCLC) has a dismal prognosis, yet there remains a lack of standardized therapeutic guidelines. While this transformation is predominantly driven by concurrent loss of TP53 and RB1, retaining wild-type RB1 is exceptionally rare. We report a rare case of RB1-wildtype T-SCLC with prolonged survival to highlight its diagnostic challenges, potential biological mechanisms, and therapeutic management.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 57-year-old non-smoking woman with no significant prior medical history presented with persistent dizziness, headaches, and vomiting. She was diagnosed with EGFR-mutant stage IV lung adenocarcinoma (LADC; EGFR L858R/R776H, PIK3CA E542K, TP53 C176F; RB1 wild-type) following surgical resection of brain metastases. Primary lung biopsy was not feasible due to deep tumor location and marked vascularity. She received sequential dacomitinib [progression-free survival (PFS): 14 months] and osimertinib (PFS: 9 months), monitored by serial imaging and dynamic serum neuron-specific enolase (NSE). Rising NSE prompted re-biopsy of a liver metastasis, confirming small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) transformation at 35 months. She then received serplulimab, anlotinib, etoposide, and carboplatin; significant tumor regression was observed after two cycles, though grade 3-4 hematologic toxicities after the third cycle resolved with supportive care. Liver progression after six cycles prompted second-line nab-paclitaxel plus serplulimab and anlotinib, achieving renewed disease control for over 3 months. Treatment adherence was generally good throughout the clinical course. Overall survival (OS) was 5 years and 4 months, with post-transformation survival of 14 months.
CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights a rare RB1-wildtype transformation from EGFR-mutant LADC to SCLC, suggesting a distinct mechanism of lineage plasticity. Dynamic NSE elevation may serve as an early clinical indicator of transformation when tissue re-biopsy is challenging. The durable response achieved with serplulimab-based chemoimmunotherapy combined with anlotinib provides preliminary support for immunotherapy-based strategies in selected patients with T-SCLC.

title: Postoperative chylothorax associated with lymphatic channels around the azygos arch after right upper lobectomy: a case report.
authors: Zhang Q, Li Z, Liu L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative chylothorax is an uncommon complication of pulmonary resection and mediastinal lymph-node dissection. Anatomical variations of the thoracic duct and its tributaries are recognized, but their clinical relevance during right superior mediastinal lymphadenectomy may be difficult to appreciate. We report a case of postoperative chylothorax associated with an intraoperative finding of two lymphatic channels around the azygos arch after induction aumolertinib therapy.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 71-year-old woman with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) L858R-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and a solitary brain metastasis underwent craniotomy followed by 3 months of induction aumolertinib. After radiographic response, she underwent uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph-node dissection. During dissection of stations 2R and 4R near the azygos arch, a translucent lymphatic channel was injured and milky fluid was observed. Further local exploration identified two separate lymphatic channels around the azygos arch; their complete course and relationship to the azygos vein could not be confirmed. The injured superior channel was ligated and clipped, whereas the inferior channel appeared intact and was not manipulated. Postoperatively, chylothorax developed, with pleural-fluid triglycerides of 524 mg/dL and drainage of 620 mL/day. Conservative treatment with nil per os, total parenteral nutrition, and intravenous somatostatin at 125 μg/hour by continuous infusion was initiated on postoperative day (POD) 1 and discontinued on POD 4. The chest tube was removed on POD 7, and no recurrent chylothorax or tumor progression was observed during 9 months of follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: This case describes an intraoperative observation of two lymphatic channels around the azygos arch during right superior mediastinal lymphadenectomy. Because no dedicated lymphatic imaging or formal anatomical confirmation was performed, the complete lymphatic course and anatomical classification of these channels remain uncertain. This observation is hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as definitive confirmation of a thoracic duct anomaly.

title: Berberine and celecoxib synergistically suppress non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR/AKT/COX-2-related signaling: network pharmacology, molecular docking and experimental validation.
authors: Wang Q, Bian C, She X et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, and safer combination strategies with improved antitumor efficacy are still needed. Berberine (BBR), a natural isoquinoline alkaloid with multi-target pharmacological activity, and celecoxib (CXB), a selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitor, have shown antitumor potential. However, their combined efficacy and underlying mechanisms in NSCLC remain unclear.
METHODS: Network pharmacology, molecular docking, Chou-Talalay combination index analysis, complementary synergy analysis using SynergyFinder+, in vitro functional assays, molecular validation, and a PC9 xenograft model were integrated to evaluate the antitumor effects and associated molecular changes of BBR combined with CXB. Candidate targets and pathways were screened using protein-protein interaction analysis, GO/KEGG enrichment, and Target-Pathway network analysis. Molecular docking was performed to assess the predicted binding affinity of BBR and CXB with key targets, and native-ligand re-docking was performed to validate the docking protocol. Cell viability, proliferation, colony formation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, and molecular changes were examined using CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, wound-healing, Transwell invasion, flow cytometry, Western blotting, qRT-PCR, immunohistochemistry, and in vivo experiments.
RESULTS: Network analysis identified EGFR, AKT1, and PTGS2 (encoding COX-2) as candidate nodes, and molecular docking suggested predicted binding of BBR and CXB with EGFR, AKT1, and COX-2. Native-ligand re-docking showed acceptable reproduction of the crystallographic ligand poses. BBR and CXB synergistically reduced A549 and PC9 cell viability, with ZIP, HSA, Loewe, and Bliss analyses further supporting the multidose synergy, and a representative working combination dose was used for validation. The combination significantly inhibited proliferation, colony formation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. These effects were accompanied by suppression of EGFR and AKT phosphorylation, reduced COX-2 expression, downregulation of TNF-α, IL-1β, and CXCL8, decreased the Bcl-2/Bax ratio, and increased cleaved-Caspase-3. In vivo, BBR + CXB more effectively inhibited PC9 xenograft growth than either monotherapy without obvious body weight loss, accompanied by reduced Ki-67, p-EGFR, p-AKT, and COX-2 expression and increased cleaved-Caspase-3 staining.
CONCLUSION: BBR combined with CXB exhibits synergistic antitumor activity in NSCLC cells and enhanced antitumor efficacy in vivo, associated with suppression of EGFR/AKT/COX-2-related signaling, attenuation of inflammatory responses, and activation of apoptosis, providing support for this potential combination strategy.

title: Dacomitinib With or Without Dose Titration in Treatment-Naive Advanced EGFR-Mutated NSCLC - Primary Analysis of the ATORG-003 Phase 2 Trial.
authors: Tan AC, Kim TM, Zhou S et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Dacomitinib is an approved second-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor. In the phase 3 ARCHER 1050 trial, both progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were improved with first-line dacomitinib compared with gefitinib. Post hoc analysis revealed that efficacy (PFS, OS) was similar in both dose-reduced patients and the overall study population. ATORG-003 evaluated a dose-titration strategy to improve tolerability while maintaining efficacy. This is also the first prospective study of dacomitinib's intracranial efficacy and resistance (tissue and plasma next-generation sequencing).
METHODS: ATORG-003 (Asian Thoracic Oncology Research Group; five Asian countries) was a single-arm, investigator-initiated phase 2 trial that enrolled patients with treatment-naive stages IIIB to IV EGFR-mutated NSCLC. Patients received dacomitinib 30 mg daily for 4 weeks, with a shared investigator and patient decision for titration to 45 mg in patients with grade less than or equal to 1 toxicity (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0). The primary end point was the 12-month PFS rate (in patients without central nervous system metastases only) compared with the historical control. Secondary end points were time to treatment failure (TTF), objective response rate (ORR), OS, intracranial ORR (iORR) and intracranial PFS (iPFS), and safety and tolerability.
RESULTS: From September 2019 to October 2022, 118 patients were enrolled. The median age was 65 (range 33-84) years, and 54% were female. EGFR mutation type was exon 19 deletion in 57%, L858R mutation in 42%, and both in 1%. There were 18% of patients who were dose titrated to 45 mg at cycle 2, and 70% tolerated 30 mg (67%) or 45 mg (3%) without dose reduction. The primary end point was met, with a 12-month PFS proportion rate of 59.6% (90% confidence interval [CI]: 50.6%-68.1%) and a 12-month PFS rate of 61.2% (95% CI: 50.5%-70.3%) in the primary analysis cohort. The median PFS was 16.1 months (95% CI: 12.1-19.2), and the median TTF was 19.3 months (95% CI: 16.1-22.1). In the overall study population, the ORR was 77% and the median OS was not reached. In patients with central nervous system metastases (n = 24), the iORR was 54% and the median iPFS was 17.6 months (95% CI: 7.2-23.1). All patients had treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs), with grade 3/4 TRAEs occurring in 25%. The most common grade 3/4 TRAEs were rash (7%), paronychia (4%), and hypokalemia (3%). EGFR T790M resistance was detected in 29 of 96 patients (30%) through plasma next-generation sequencing and in 15 of 29 patients (52%) through tissue next-generation sequencing.
CONCLUSION: ATORG-003 prospectively revealed that dacomitinib with dose titration is a viable strategy in advanced EGFR-mutated NSCLC, maintaining efficacy while improving tolerability. Dacomitinib has substantial intracranial activity and high rates of T790M resistance, making it suitable for sequential treatment approaches.

title: Synergistic effects and molecular mechanisms of pirfenidone combined with EGFR-TKIs in non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Tang P, Huang C, Zhang F et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally. While epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), such as osimertinib (OS) and afatinib (AF), have markedly improved clinical outcomes, their efficacy is significantly hindered by the development of acquired resistance. Emerging evidence suggests that p38γ is involved in the progression of NSCLC and the emergence of resistance to EGFR-TKIs. However, whether the p38γ inhibitor pirfenidone (PFD) can enhance the sensitivity of NSCLC to EGFR-TKIs remains unclear. This study aims to evaluate the synergistic antitumor effects of PFD in combination with OS or AF and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.
METHODS: EGFR-mutant NSCLC cell lines (PC9 and HCC827) and their OS-resistant derivatives (HCC827 OR) were utilized to evaluate cell proliferation by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assays and colony formation experiments. Western blotting was performed to analyze the expression of p38γ, proteins within the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) signaling pathway, and autophagy-related markers. Drug interactions were assessed using the SynergyFinder platform. Autophagic flux was investigated via a dual-fluorescent adenovirus (mRFP-GFP-LC3) and further validated using the autophagy inhibitor bafilomycin A1. Additionally, an HCC827 nude mouse xenograft model was employed for in vivo validation.
RESULTS: The combination of PFD with either OS or AF exhibited significant synergistic antitumor effects in both in vitro and in vivo NSCLC models, consistently achieving Bliss synergy scores exceeding 14. Notably, this combination successfully restored drug sensitivity in OS-resistant cells and reversed acquired resistance to EGFR-TKIs. Mechanistic investigations revealed that PFD enhanced EGFR-TKI sensitivity via two distinct pathways: firstly, by specifically inhibiting p38γ, a critical mediator of resistance, which leads to the downregulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway; and secondly, by promoting the autophagy cascade in a p38γ-independent manner. These synergistic effects were not reversed by ferroptosis or pyroptosis inhibitors and were only partially attributed to apoptosis.
CONCLUSIONS: PFD enhances the efficacy of EGFR-TKIs through a dual mechanism: first, by specifically inhibiting the p38γ-mediated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, and second, by activating a p38γ-independent autophagy pathway. The activation of the p38γ-mediated PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway may represent a key mechanism underlying OS resistance. This study provides the first evidence that PFD can restore drug sensitivity in OS-resistant cells, offering valuable experimental support for its potential clinical application as an EGFR-TKI sensitizer and a therapeutic strategy to overcome resistance in targeted cancer therapies.

title: Retrospective real-world associations between EGFR alterations and furmonertinib outcomes in advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Cui Y, Zhou S, Liu Z et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Furmonertinib, a third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI), has shown promising efficacy in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This real-world study aimed to explore efficacy differences among EGFR mutation subtypes and the influence of concomitant genetic alterations on furmonertinib.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter real-world study enrolled patients with unresectable stage IIIB/C-IV EGFR-mutant NSCLC who received furmonertinib (80 milligrams per day). Main eligibility criteria included advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC, measurable lesions, and available next-generation sequencing (NGS) molecular data. Patients were recruited from five Chinese medical centers. Progression-free survival (PFS) was defined as time from furmonertinib initiation to disease progression or any-cause death; overall survival (OS) was defined as time from furmonertinib initiation to any-cause death or last follow-up. Baseline clinical and NGS-detected molecular data were collected. Survival endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), disease control rates (DCRs), PFS and OS. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional-hazards models were applied to evaluate prognostic associations, reporting hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) alongside exact P values.
RESULTS: A total of 139 patients were included, among whom 64 harbored EGFR exon 19 deletion and 74 harbored L858R mutation. TP53 mutations were detected in 64.4% (58/90) of the tested patients. There were 136 patients profiled for additional concurrent driver alterations. Among 131 evaluable patients, ORR was 69.5% and the DCR was 97.7%. Median PFS of the entire cohort was 623 days (approximately 20.8 months); median OS was not reached. Compared with L858R, EGFR exon19 deletion was associated with longer PFS (adjusted HR =1.77, 95% CI: 1.09-2.87, P=0.02). After adjusting for age, disease stage, and EGFR mutation subtype, multiple gene mutations were associated with poorer PFS (HR =4.03, 95% CI: 1.98-8.19, P<0.001) and OS (HR =3.25, 95% CI: 1.07-9.86, P=0.04). No significant prognostic association was observed for TP53 co-mutation.
CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective real-world cohort suggests that EGFR subtypes and multiple concurrent genomic alterations are associated with survival outcomes under furmonertinib treatment.

title: Synchronous lung adenocarcinoma and pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets in different lobes: a case report.
authors: Li YQ, Xu YZ
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets are small (< 5 mm) neuroendocrine proliferations that are usually identified incidentally in resected lung tissue. Their coexistence with a spatially separate lung adenocarcinoma is uncommon and may complicate the interpretation of multiple pulmonary nodules.
CASE SUMMARY: A 71-year-old woman with multiple bilateral pulmonary micronodules that had remained radiologically stable for approximately 2 years was admitted after a newly detected lesion in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe was considered suspicious for lung cancer. She reported occasional chest tightness and intermittent cough with sputum and had never smoked. Bronchoscopy and brush cytology were negative. The patient underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left upper lobe lesion. Frozen-section examination showed adenocarcinoma, prompting a left upper lobectomy with systematic lymph-node dissection. A left lower lobe wedge resection was performed to sample representative micronodules. Final pathology showed a 3.0-cm invasive adenocarcinoma (approximately 80% acinar and 20% lepidic patterns), without visceral pleural, definite vascular invasion, or metastasis in 17 sampled lymph nodes (pT1cN0M0, stage IA3). The left lower lobe nodules were reported as pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets and were positive for AE1/AE3, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, CD56, and TTF-1, with a Ki-67 index of approximately 2%. The adenocarcinoma harbored an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation. She was discharged 1 week after surgery.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that pulmonary micronodules accompanying a dominant lung cancer may represent a separate neuroendocrine proliferation rather than intrapulmonary metastases. Diagnosis requires correlation of lesion size, morphology, and immunophenotype. Unsampled contralateral nodules could remain radiologically indeterminate and undergo structured surveillance.

title: Bioelectrical impedance-derived body composition and systemic therapy outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Zheng X, Gao R, Jiang B et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Body mass index (BMI) cannot distinguish skeletal muscle from adipose tissue or capture fat distribution in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We explored whether bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-assessed body composition was associated with systemic therapy outcomes.
METHODS: Consecutive adults with confirmed NSCLC who underwent pretreatment multifrequency BIA between March 2023 and March 2025 were retrospectively included. Analyses were performed by treatment context, including stage I surgical patients and stage II-IV patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)- or epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI)-based systemic therapy. Body-composition parameters were compared by clinical stage and EGFR mutation status using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA). Progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. Objective response rate (ORR) was evaluated using logistic regression. Joint analyses were performed according to skeletal muscle index (SMI) and visceral fat index (VFI), and longitudinal body-composition changes during immunotherapy were also assessed.
RESULTS: Among 473 screened patients, 369 were included, comprising 126 with stage I disease and 243 with stage II-IV disease. After predefined exclusions, outcome cohorts included 125 ICI-treated and 43 EGFR-TKI-treated patients. In cross-sectional analyses, adiposity-related parameters were nominally lower in stage II-IV disease than in stage I disease, but these differences did not remain significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction; no body-composition parameter differed significantly by EGFR mutation status. Among 94 men included in the primary ICI PFS analysis, high SMI was associated with longer PFS [adjusted hazard ratio (HR), 0.49; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.25-0.97], whereas high VFI was associated with shorter PFS (adjusted HR, 2.11; 95% CI: 1.09-4.07). High SMI was also associated with higher ORR among these men [adjusted odds ratio (OR), 3.04; 95% CI: 1.20-7.72]. The combined SMI/VFI phenotype further stratified PFS, with low SMI/high VFI identifying the least favorable subgroup. In an exploratory longitudinal analysis, a >10% decrease in trunk fat mass was associated with shorter PFS. No clear associations between body-composition parameters and PFS were observed in the small EGFR-TKI cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: BIA-assessed skeletal muscle reserve and visceral adiposity were associated with outcomes during ICI-based therapy in men with NSCLC. Higher SMI and lower VFI identified a more favorable clinical profile. Prospective validation is warranted to define the role of BIA-based body-composition assessment in host-related risk stratification during systemic therapy.

title: Integrating multimodal data for precise subtyping and prognostication in patients with pulmonary mucinous adenocarcinoma.
authors: Yang W, Chen C, Li L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary mucinous adenocarcinoma (PMA) represents a rare lung adenocarcinoma subtype, characterized by a lack of comprehensive pathological classification and prognostic factors. In this study, we propose a multimodal machine learning (ML) framework that integrates multiple data modalities to enhance PMA subtype classification and prognostic prediction.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 175 primary PMA cases with details of demographic, histopathological, computed tomography (CT) imaging, and epithelial growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation data. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regularized logistic regression model was utilized for histological classification, and Cox proportional hazards model was employed for survival prediction with internal validation.
RESULTS: Pure mucinous adenocarcinoma presented a higher prevalence of smaller radiographic or pathological tumor size, lower lobe localization, lower rates of lymph node metastasis and spread through air spaces (STAS), early pathological stage, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) ≤5 ng/mL, spiculated margin, Ki-67 low expression and lower frequency of EGFR exon 19 deletion (P=0.002, 0.003, <0.001, <0.001, 0.001, <0.001, 0.002, 0.03, 0.02, 0.001, respectively) compared to mix mucinous and mucin-secreting adenocarcinoma. The ML-derived nomogram achieved discriminative ability, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.792 in the training set and 0.687 in the validation set, and exhibited satisfactory calibration for the preoperative diagnosis of pure mucinous adenocarcinoma. Multivariate Cox modeling identified higher CEA levels, and EGFR exon 19 deletion as independent prognostic factors in PMA (P=0.04, 0.049, respectively). Moreover, Kaplan-Meier curves revealed significantly different outcomes between low- and high-risk groups stratified by the nomogram score (P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Pulmonary pure mucinous adenocarcinoma exhibited lower malignancy compared to the mixed mucinous and mucin-secreting type. The nomogram model developed and validated in this study exhibited promising efficacy in predicting histological subtype preoperatively and survival in patients with PMA, offering guidance for clinicians in diagnosis and prognosis prediction.

title: Efficacy and safety of osimertinib combined with anlotinib in EGFR-mutant non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer with gradual progression after first-line osimertinib therapy: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
authors: Hao L, Yu H, Wang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osimertinib, a third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), has substantially improved clinical outcomes in patients with EGFR-mutant non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Nevertheless, acquired resistance inevitably develops, leading to disease progression in the majority of patients. Preclinical and clinical evidence suggests that anlotinib, a multi-targeted anti-angiogenic TKI, may overcome osimertinib resistance. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of continued osimertinib in combination with anlotinib in patients with EGFR-mutant non-squamous NSCLC who developed gradual progression following first-line osimertinib therapy.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable stage III or IV EGFR-mutant non-squamous NSCLC who received first-line osimertinib therapy at The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China between January 2021 and December 2024. Eligible patients developed gradual progression after first-line osimertinib therapy. Subsequently, patients received combination therapy with osimertinib (80 mg orally once daily) plus anlotinib (10 mg orally on days 1-14 of every 3-week cycle). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included PFS rates at 6 and 12 months, objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS), OS rates at 12 and 24 months, and safety profile.
RESULTS: A total of 52 patients were enrolled. The median age was 66 years. 40(76.9%) had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) of 0-1, 16 (30.8%) presented with brain metastases, 23 (44.2%) harbored exon 19 deletions, and 29 (55.8%) had L858R mutations. Molecular testing was performed in 12 patients after gradual progression. As of September 6, 2025, the median follow-up was 34.8 months, 48 PFS events were recorded and 22 patients died. The ORR was 7.7% (4/52), and the DCR was 86.5% (45/52). The median PFS (mPFS) was 9.9 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 4.2-12.1], with PFS rates of 61.5% at 6 months and 40.4% at 12 months. The median OS was not reached. OS rates were 86.3% at 12 months and 62.4% at 24 months. The exploratory multivariate COX analysis revealed that ECOG PS [hazard ratio (HR): 3.115, 95% CI: 1.111-7.706, P<0.001] and brain metastasis (HR: 2.242, 95% CI: 1.341-7.842, P=0.009) were associated with mPFS. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 9.6% (5/52) of patients. The most frequently observed AEs were diarrhea (42.3%, 22/52), hypertension (34.6%, 18/52), proteinuria (30.8%, 16/52), decreased appetite (28.8%, 15/52), and weight loss (28.8%, 15/52).
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort focusing on the specific pattern of gradual progression following first-line osimertinib therapy, continued osimertinib combined with anlotinib demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity, which warrants further evaluation in prospective comparative studies.

title: Efficacy and safety of third-generation EGFR-TKI rechallenge therapy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer patients with EGFR mutation: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Sun J, Li X, Wang B et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have become the standard treatment for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but acquired resistance remains inevitable. Current post-progression salvage regimens offer only modest clinical benefits, leaving an unmet need for effective late-line treatment strategies. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of third-generation EGFR-TKI rechallenge as a potential salvage option for heavily pretreated resistant NSCLC patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 29 patients with advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC who received third-generation EGFR-TKI rechallenge after progression on prior third-generation EGFR-TKI therapy between December 2019 and August 2025. All patients had pathologically confirmed EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and received multi-line subsequent treatment after third-generation EGFR-TKIs resistance. Baseline clinical data were extracted from electronic medical records, and follow-up chest CT evaluations were conducted every 6 to 8 weeks. Outcomes were standardized using RECIST version 1.1 for tumor responses and CTCAE version 5.0 for adverse events. Survival outcomes [progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS)] were analyzed via Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. The primary endpoint was PFS. Secondary endpoints included OS and disease control rate (DCR).
RESULTS: The median number of prior systemic treatment lines was 5 (range, 3-12). Third-generation EGFR-TKI rechallenge achieved a median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 6.0 months, a median overall survival (mOS) of 12.0 months. The DCR was 6/29 (20.7%). Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 8/29 (27.6%) patients, with severe (grade ≥3) events in 3/29 (10.3%). Poorer baseline ECOG PS (3-4) was significantly associated with inferior PFS (median: 5.0 vs. 7.0 months, P=0.04) and OS (median: 10.0 vs. 25.0 months, P=0.005). Chemotherapy-containing interval therapy was associated with improved PFS (7.5 vs. 2.0 months, P=0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Third-generation EGFR-TKI rechallenge may provide a feasible and well-tolerated salvage option for selected heavily pretreated patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC. ECOG PS and prior treatment patterns may assist in patient selection for rechallenge therapy. However, these findings are strictly exploratory and require validation in larger, controlled prospective studies.

title: Amivantamab plus chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutant advanced non-small cell lung cancer after progression on osimertinib: a MARIPOSA-2 analysis of the Asian subgroup.
authors: Shih JY, Wang J, Wang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Phase 3 MARIPOSA-2 study showed that amivantamab, a bispecific antibody with immune cell-directing activity, plus chemotherapy significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) compared with chemotherapy alone in participants with common epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), whose disease had progressed on osimertinib monotherapy. We conducted a post hoc analysis to assess clinical outcomes in the Asian subgroup of participants from MARIPOSA-2 (NCT04988295).
METHODS: Participants were randomised 2:2:1 to amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy, chemotherapy alone, or amivantamab-chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was PFS by blinded independent central review (BICR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1 (RECIST 1.1). Secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), intracranial PFS, and safety. Due to mid-study modifications to the amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy dosing schedule, follow-up of this group is ongoing. We present results for the amivantamab-chemotherapy vs. chemotherapy arms in the Asian subgroup.
RESULTS: There were 190 participants in the Asian subgroup, 63 in the amivantamab-chemotherapy group and 127 in the chemotherapy group. At a median follow-up of 9.5 months, median PFS in the amivantamab-chemotherapy arm was 6.8 vs. 4.2 months in the chemotherapy arm [hazard ratio (HR) 0.54, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.37-0.81; nominal P=0.002]. The ORR was 66% and 32%, respectively (odds ratio 4.0, 95% CI: 2.1-7.7; nominal P<0.001) and median intracranial PFS was 12.5 and 8.5 months (HR 0.58, 95% CI: 0.34-1.00; nominal P=0.049). The safety profile in the Asian subgroup was in line with the overall MARIPOSA-2 population.
CONCLUSIONS: Amivantamab-chemotherapy demonstrated superior PFS vs. chemotherapy in Asian patients. Amivantamab-chemotherapy provides an effective option for patients whose disease had progressed on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors.

title: Cellular immunotherapy for lung cancer: current clinical evidence, translational challenges, and future perspectives: a narrative review.
authors: Ma N, Shang C
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Cellular immunotherapy has achieved major advances in hematologic malignancies, but translation to lung cancer is constrained by antigen heterogeneity, limited trafficking and persistence, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), manufacturing complexity, and on-target off-tumor toxicity. This narrative review summarizes current clinical evidence, major translational barriers, and future development strategies for cellular immunotherapy in lung cancer.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from database inception to 1 June 2026 using Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and free-text terms. Evidence on chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T), T-cell receptor-engineered T-cell (TCR-T), tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL), natural killer (NK), chimeric antigen receptor natural killer (CAR-NK), and cancer vaccine-based strategies was reviewed, with priority given to non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small-cell lung cancer (SCLC).
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Most lung-cancer cellular therapy studies remain early phase. TIL therapy has demonstrated clinical activity in NSCLC, while EGFR, MSLN, CEA, MUC1, PD-L1, B7-H3, and DLL3 are representative targets under investigation for CAR-based approaches; NY-ESO-1 and KK-LC-1 are representative TCR-T targets. Major barriers include antigen escape, poor tumor infiltration, HLA restriction or loss, immunosuppressive signaling, cellular exhaustion, limited persistence, manufacturing burden, and treatment-related toxicity. Current optimization strategies include gene editing, chemokine-receptor engineering, armored or logic-gated receptors, safety switches, optimized lymphodepletion, and rational combinations with other anticancer therapies.
CONCLUSIONS: Cellular immunotherapy is a promising but still developing strategy for lung cancer. Future studies should prioritize biomarker-guided patient selection, safer and more persistent cell products, scalable manufacturing, and prospective clinical validation of rational combination strategies.

title: [Mechanistic study on Kaixin Powder ameliorating chronic stress-induced CD8~+T cell exhaustion and delaying lung adenocarcinoma progression by modulating IDO1/Kyn/Ahr axis].
authors: Fu X, Bai YT, He JW et al.
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the interventional effects of Kaixin Powder(KXP) on the progression of lung adenocarcinoma(LUAD) under chronic stress and its underlying mechanism. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry(UPLC-MS/MS) was employed to characterize the chemical constituents of KXP, followed by network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses to screen for its potential targets. A chronic stress-associated lung cancer mouse model was established by axillary inoculation of Lewis lung carcinoma(LLC) cells combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress(CUMS). Sixty SPF-grade C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into the following groups: normal group, lung cancer group, model group, low-and high-dose KXP(13.65 and 27.3 g·kg~(-1)) groups, and fluoxetine(2 mg·kg~(-1)) group. Tumor growth indicators, including body weight, tumor mass, and tumor inhibition rate of mice were measured. Depression-like behaviors were observed by open field test(OFT) and sucrose preference test(SPT). Serum levels of stress factors such as corticosterone(Cort) and kynurenine(Kyn) were measured by ELISA. Histopathological changes in tumor tissue were assessed by hematoxylin-eosin(HE) staining. Peripheral blood T lymphocyte subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry. Intratumoral CD8~+T cells infiltration was detected by immunofluorescence, and the protein expression levels of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1(IDO1) and aryl hydrocarbon receptor(Ahr) were determined by Western blot. Serum ALT, AST, BUN, and Scr levels were measured to evaluate hepatic and renal safety. UPLC-MS/MS analysis characterized 157 chemical constituents of KXP. The protein expression levels of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1(IDO1) and aryl hydrocarbon receptor(Ahr) were detected by Western blot. In addition, serum ALT, AST, BUN, and Scr levels were measured to evaluate hepatic and renal safety. UPLC-MS identified 157 chemical constituents of KXP. Network pharmacology analysis obtained 367 potential targets, among which epidermal growth factor receptor(EGFR), protein kinase B alpha(AKT1), signal transducer and activator of transcription 3(STAT3), heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1(HSP90AA1), and IDO1 were screened as core targets. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes(KEGG) pathway analysis and molecular docking indicated that abnormal tryptophan metabolism mediated by IDO1 may be a potential mechanism underlying KXP intervention in LUAD complicated with depression. Animal experiments showed that, compared with the lung cancer group, the model group exhibited significantly accelerated tumor growth, increased structural disarray and atypia in HE-stained tumor tissue, obvious depression-like behaviors, and significantly elevated serum Cort and Kyn levels. In addition, the proportions of peripheral blood CD3~+ and CD3~+CD4~+T cells and the CD3~+CD4~+/CD3~+CD8~+ ratio significantly decreased, whereas the proportion of CD3~+CD8~+T cells significantly increased. Intratumoral CD8~+T cells infiltration was reduced, while the protein expression levels of IDO1 and Ahr were significantly upregulated. Compared with the model group, the high-dose KXP group showed significantly reduced tumor volume and tumor weight, with a tumor inhibition rate of 52.43%. KXP intervention improved depression-like behaviors to varying degrees, with the high-dose group showing more pronounced improvements in OFT activity indicators and SPT sucrose preference rate. Serum Cort and Kyn levels were significantly reduced in the high-dose KXP group. The proportions of peripheral blood CD3~+ and CD3~+CD4~+T cells and the CD3~+CD4~+/CD3~+CD8~+ ratio significantly increased in both low-and high-dose KXP groups. The low-dose KXP group showed significantly reduced IDO1 protein expression, while the high-dose group showed significantly reduced expression of both IDO1 and Ahr proteins. Safety evaluation showed that, within the experimental dose range, KXP had no obvious adverse effects on the morphology of major organs or on serum ALT, AST, BUN, and Scr levels. In conclusion, KXP ameliorates chronic stress and delays LUAD progression, and its mechanism may be associated with inhibition of the IDO1/Kyn/Ahr axis, correction of abnormal tryptophan metabolism, promotion of intratumoral CD8~+T cells infiltration, and improvement of the tumor immune microenvironment.

title: Emerging landscape of antibody-drug conjugates in lung cancer: a clinical review.
authors: Pickett H, Arias-Romero J, Fricke J et al.
abstract: Lung cancer is a heterogeneous disease, and while targeted therapies and immunotherapies have improved patient outcomes, 5-year overall survival remains poor at approximately 20%. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) target tumors using a targeted antibody that delivers a cytotoxic payload with clinically proven antitumor activity, and over a dozen ADCs are under consideration for solid tumors. Recent clinical trial data in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer have led to FDA approval of three ADCs: trastuzumab deruxtecan for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-mutated disease, telisotuzumab vedotin for MET-overexpressing tumors, and datopotamab deruxtecan for patients with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated disease. In this article, we review the trajectory of individual ADC targets in lung cancer, describe the latest clinical trial results, and discuss future innovations in ADC therapies and potential mechanisms of resistance.

title: Inhibition of the MEK-ERK signaling pathway reverses acquired osimertinib resistance in NSCLC attributed to AXL overexpression.
authors: Zhang K, Yu X, Liu Y et al.
abstract: Osimertinib, a third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI), is the standard first-line treatment for patients with EGFR-activating mutation of late-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the emergence of acquired resistance limits its efficacy in real use. The overexpression of anexelekto (AXL) is known to be associated with acquired resistance to osimertinib. However, the specific mechanisms of AXL-mediated resistance are not well explained, nor of the specific therapeutic approaches in patients for this. In this study, we identified that activation of MEK-ERK pathway played a key role in AXL-driven acquired osimertinib resistance in NSCLC. Inhibition of the MEK-ERK activation restored osimertinib sensitivity in AXL-driven resistant tumor cells. The combination use of MEK inhibitor with osimertinib reversed the aquierd osimertinib resistance in vitor and in vivo. Our findings provide preclinical mechanistic support for potential use to targeting MEK-ERK signaling in AXL-associated osimertinib resistance and forfurther validation in patient-derived and clinical models.

title: Xanthatin overcomes osimertinib resistance by disturbing cholesterol metabolism via targeting HMGCR protein degradation in NSCLC.
authors: Yuan H, Wang G, Li L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is a third-generation, irreversible EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), nevertheless, the inevitable occurrence of osimertinib resistance after a long-term administration limits its clinical application in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Xanthatin, a naturally active component from Xanthium Strumarium L., has been shown to possess multiple bioactive effects. However, whether xanthatin can ameliorate osimertinib resistance remains unclear.
PURPOSE: The present study aimed to clarify the role and detailed mechanism of xanthatin in reversing osimertinib resistance in NSCLC.
METHODS: Combenefit analysis, LDH release assay, and EdU staining were employed to evaluate the effect of xanthatin on osimertinib cytotoxicity in osimertinib-resistant (OR) NSCLC cells. Quantitative proteomics combined with bioinformatics and network pharmacology analysis was used to uncover the specific target of xanthatin. Xanthatin-triggered HMGCR protein degradation was assessed by bio-layer interferometry, drug affinity responsive target stability assay, cycloheximide chase assay and ubiquitination determination. The function of xanthatin on cholesterol homeostasis was measured via the detection of HMGCR activity, total cholesterol, triglycerides and lipid droplets as well as MDR1 distribution in the lipid rafts. The function of MDR1 was examined via a rhodamine 123 efflux assay. The accumulation and efflux of osimertinib were monitored using FITC-labeled osimertinib. The effect of HMGCR on the cytotoxicity of xanthatin was evaluated through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments in HMGCR-overexpressing NSCLC OR cells.
RESULTS: Xanthatin restored the sensitivity of NSCLC OR cells to osimertinib, accompanied by the induction of oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Proteomic data indicate that oxidative stress and metabolic reprogramming contribute to xanthatin-induced apoptosis in NSCLC OR cells. Through further integration with network pharmacology, we identified HMGCR (a key enzyme of cholesterol metabolism) as a potential target of xanthatin. We confirmed xanthatin directly binds to HMGCR protein (KD=6.753 μM), subsequently facilitating AMFR-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of HMGCR. Xanthatin diminished intracellular cholesterol biosynthesis and MDR1 levels in lipid rafts. HMGCR overexpression mitigated the cytotoxicity of xanthatin and sustained cholesterol homeostasis, enabling tolerance to the combined effects of xanthatin and osimertinib. Conversely, HMGCR-deficient NSCLC OR cells were more vulnerable to osimertinib.
CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates for the first time that xanthatin directly binds to HMGCR and promotes AMFR-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination of HMGCR, which in turn accelerates HMGCR degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, leading to reduced cholesterol synthesis, less distribution of MDR1 in lipid rafts, ROS accumulation, and mitochondrial dysfunction-associated apoptosis, ultimately restoring osimertinib sensitivity in NSCLC cells. Therefore, xanthatin may represent a preclinical natural product candidate for the reversal of osimertinib resistance in NSCLC cells, which requires further translational verification in future studies.

title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel aminopyrimidine derivatives as potent EGFRC797S inhibitors for overcoming osimertinib resistance.
authors: Wang Y, Ma L, Huang R et al.
abstract: EGFRC797S mutation and bypass pathway activation are major drivers of acquired resistance to osimertinib; however, no approved therapeutic agents are currently available to effectively overcome this resistance. In this study, a series of aminopyrimidine-based small-molecule inhibitors were rationally designed and synthesized. The lead compound 6a exhibits potent single-digit nanomolar activity against EGFRL858R/T790M/C797S (IC50 = 1.76 nM), along with equipotent ALK inhibitory activity (IC50 = 1.95 nM) that may address ALK-mediated bypass resistance. The co-crystal structure of EGFRC797S in complex with 6a (PDB: 9XU9) reveals a unique hydrogen bond between the inhibitor and Ser797-the residue that confers osimertinib resistance-providing a structural basis for resistance overcoming. In cellular assays, 6a potently inhibits proliferation of osimertinib-resistant H1975-M3 cells (IC50 = 0.035 μM), suppresses downstream oncogenic signaling, induces G0/G1 cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, and impairs cell migration and invasion. In vivo, 6a demonstrates robust antitumor efficacy in an H1975-M3 xenograft model with a tumor growth inhibition rate of 86.47% at 30 mg/kg, significantly outperforming brigatinib (55.53%), while exhibiting favorable safety and pharmacokinetic profiles. Collectively, these findings establish 6a as a promising therapeutic candidate for overcoming osimertinib resistance.

title: A Podcast on Osimertinib After CRT in Unresectable Stage III EGFR-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC): Current and Future Perspectives.
authors: Reungwetwattana T, Higgins KA, Casarini I et al.
abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated (EGFRm) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) disease biology may differ from EGFR-wild type NSCLC, with an increased risk of distant metastases in unresectable stage III EGFRm NSCLC. Osimertinib is an established first treatment for patients with EGFRm advanced NSCLC, effectively treating EGFRm tumours. The phase III LAURA study, which assessed the efficacy and safety of osimertinib for patients with locally advanced, unresectable stage III EGFRm NSCLC who completed chemoradiotherapy (CRT) without disease progression, demonstrated a statistically significant improvement with osimertinib in progression-free survival (PFS), with a median PFS of 39.1 months, versus 5.6 months with placebo. The safety profile was as expected based on the known profiles of osimertinib and CRT. On the basis of the LAURA results, osimertinib has now been approved for the treatment of unresectable stage III EGFRm NSCLC. Given the implementation of the LAURA regimen in multiple countries, this podcast highlights the potential challenges that must be considered by healthcare professionals when administering osimertinib in clinical practice, and how these may be mitigated. Considerations of the impact of the 'treat-to-progression' approach, a paradigm shift for the treatment of stage III unresectable NSCLC, and patient-centred care, including the importance of shared decision-making, will also be discussed. Overall, continuous systemic treatment post-CRT may be key to improving long-term outcomes and represents a mindset shift for both healthcare professionals and patients. Therefore, we may need to consider unresectable stage III EGFRm NSCLC as a chronic disease, requiring long-term treatment to maintain suppression of disease.The podcast and transcript can be viewed below the abstract of the online version of the manuscript. Alternatively, the podcast can be downloaded here: https://doi.org/ https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.33191613 . Supplementary file1 (MP4 306769 KB).

title: MRD-Guided Aumolertinib-Based Adjuvant Therapy for Resected EGFR-Mutant NSCLC
summary:
Despite complete (R0) resection, patients with EGFR-mutant stage IIA-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) still face a substantial risk of postoperative recurrence. Although adjuvant EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors have improved disease-free survival, conventional fixed-duration adjuvant therapy is applied uniformly to all patients and does not distinguish those who genuinely require treatment from those who could be safely spared. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) profiling enables minimal residual disease (MRD) detection that is both earlier and more accurate than imaging, and has therefore emerged as a promising tool for individualizing postoperative adjuvant therapy.

This prospective, real-world, interventional study will enroll 50 patients with resected (R0), EGFR 19del or L858R mutant, stage IIA-IIIB non-squamous NSCLC. For three years after surgery, adjuvant treatment is dynamically guided by serial MRD testing performed 3-10 days and 4 weeks (±7 days) after surgery and every 3-6 months thereafter. Patients with a positive MRD result at either of the first two time points receive aumolertinib-based adjuvant therapy, with the regimen determined by the mutations detected in blood: aumolertinib monotherapy (110 mg once daily) when only the EGFR mutation is detected, or aumolertinib combined with chemotherapy (pemetrexed plus carboplatin for four cycles, followed by pemetrexed maintenance) when co-mutations are detected. Patients whose MRD remains negative undergo observation with regular ctDNA monitoring; if MRD turns positive or imaging progression occurs, aumolertinib-based adjuvant therapy is initiated according to the same rules. Treatment is discontinued once MRD becomes undetectable; patients with persistently negative MRD over three years receive no aumolertinib. After three years, subsequent treatment is at the investigator's discretion.

title: ACKR3 Establishes a Squamous-Restricted Immune Checkpoint Axis in Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
authors: Karatza A, Kumru K, Powell JM et al.
abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) is an aggressive subtype of non-small cell lung cancer with limited targeted therapeutic options and incompletely defined immune-regulatory dependencies. Here, we identified atypical chemokine receptor 3 (ACKR3) as a squamous-enriched regulator that restrains malignant progression in LUSC. Integrative analyses of human LUSC datasets, autochthonous genetically engineered mouse models, and ex vivo organoid systems showed that ACKR3 loss accelerated tumor growth and remodeled the immune microenvironment, marked by reduced CD8⁺ T cell infiltration and increased T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, ACKR3 limited activation of the MIF-CD74-PD-L1 axis, thereby constraining tumor-cell PD-L1 expression and preserving antitumor immune surveillance. In preclinical LUSC models, treatment with the ACKR3-directed PD-L1 degrader KineTAC, a bispecific molecule that co-engages ACKR3 and PD-L1 to promote lysosomal degradation of PD-L1, enhanced antitumor efficacy, particularly in combination with chemotherapy. Together, these findings define ACKR3 as a squamous-associated immune checkpoint regulator and nominate ACKR3-directed PD-L1 degradation as a tumor-selective therapeutic strategy for LUSC.

title: Activity and specificity of KRAS variants-directed Revolution Medicines Company (RMC) compounds for pleural effusion-derived non-small cell lung cancer cell lines.
authors: Stickler S, Eggerstorfer MT, Rieche M et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical therapy for KRAS G12C mutated lung cancers has been revolutionized by the approval of the covalent inhibitors Sotorasib and Adagrasib. However, the restriction to KRAS G12C, the response rates of approximately 45% and the duration of response (DOR) of approximately 1 year leaves room for improvements. A completely new approach uses intracellular glues to block KRAS variants by steric hindrance through binding of cyclophilin A (CYPA) to the switch regions of KRAS. A series of Revolution Medicines Company (RMC) compounds were developed, targeting all KRAS variants and KRAS wildtype, namely (RMC-6236, daraxonrasib), KRAS G12C (RMC-6291, elironrasib), KRAS G12D (RMC-9805, zoldonrasib) and KRAS G12V (RMC-5217) with more agents under development. This study aimed to reveal the specificity of RMC compounds and to discover underlying resistance mechanisms in real-world tumor cell lines.
METHODS: Four RMC compounds were tested against a panel of 22 tumor cell lines, including 15 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) lines carrying a range of KRAS mutations that were recently established from pleural effusions of lung cancer patients. Compounds were used in cytotoxicity tests and Western blot arrays comprising oncology-related proteins as well as for KRAS Western blots.
RESULTS: The RMC compounds were highly active against the wild-type KRAS cell lines but showed limited activity against the KRAS variant cell lines with approximately 50% of the NSCLC lines surviving even at the highest concentration of 2 µM with. The distinct RMC compounds targeting KRAS G12C, G12D and G12V exhibited poor selectivity for the respective NSCLC cell lines, although phosphoproteome analysis showed a uniform downregulation of the phosphorylation of ERK1/2. Cells exposed to RMC-6236 exhibited increased resistance to this drug and Western blots of KRAS revealed either increased protein expression or a shift of KRAS likely attributed to monoubiquitylation that was reported to increase KRAS activity.
CONCLUSIONS: The RMC compounds directed at KRAS G12C, D and V mutations exhibit cytotoxic activity against the correspondingly mutated newly established NSCLC cell lines und suppress the MAPK pathway. However, a significant fraction of the cancer cells survives at high drug concentrations and in most cases, the compounds show a poor selectivity for the targeted variant cell lines although they partially contain specific warheads. Increased resistance to RMC-6236 has been associated with elevated expression or likely monoubiquitylation of KRAS. The limited activity of the RMC KRAS(ON) compounds may be supplemented by conventional KRAS(OFF) compounds or other glues or degraders.

title: Efficacy and safety of antibody-drug conjugates in advanced small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of prospective clinical trials.
authors: Zhang P, Zhao W, Ma J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are being evaluated in advanced small cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the available trials include different targets, constructs, doses, and treatment settings. We aimed to determine the overall range of reported activity and safety while clarifying whether the evidence supports a clinically uniform ADC class effect.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), clinical-trial registries, and major oncology conference proceedings were searched from inception through July 31, 2026. Eligibility was restricted to reports with sufficient methodological and outcome information available in English; study country, recruitment region, investigator nationality, and participant ethnicity were not exclusion criteria. Prospective phase I-III studies of ADC monotherapy in adults with advanced, extensive-stage, relapsed, or refractory SCLC were eligible; no comparator was required, and only the ADC arm of comparative trials contributed to the single-arm synthesis. Outcomes were objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and clinically important safety events. Randomized trials were assessed using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool and non-comparative studies using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS). Random-effects models were used, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Eighteen prospective studies comprising 20 analytic cohorts and 2,246 patients were included: 12 phase I/Ib/I-II studies, three phase II studies, and three phase III studies. The pooled ORR was 34.38% [95% confidence interval (CI): 24.96-44.43%; I2=95.3%], and the pooled DCR was 77.50% (95% CI: 67.98-85.81%; I2=94.7%). The pooled median DOR, PFS, and OS were 4.99 months (95% CI: 4.24-5.86; I2=77.2%), 4.36 months (95% CI: 3.87-4.92; I2=84.8%), and 7.48 months (95% CI: 6.15-9.10; I2=92.6%), respectively. Subgroup analyses by intervention and target indicated substantial clinical and statistical heterogeneity. Safety was summarized by individual agent, dose, and source population because adverse-event definitions and denominators were not sufficiently comparable; the predominant hematologic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, and neurologic signals varied among products. Cochrane risk-of-bias judgments were predominantly low risk, with selected domains rated unclear or high risk. MINORS scores ranged from 11 to 15 of 16, with recurrent limitations in consecutive enrollment, blinded endpoint assessment, follow-up reporting, and prospective sample-size calculation.
CONCLUSIONS: ADC-based therapy shows antitumor activity in advanced SCLC, but substantial clinical and pharmacological heterogeneity limits the interpretation of pooled single-arm estimates. Agent-specific randomized trials with standardized efficacy, safety, and biomarker reporting are needed.

title: Machine Learning, Radiomics, and Clinical Models Predicting Checkpoint Inhibitor Pneumonitis in Lung Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
authors: He F, Liu G, Ye H et al.
abstract: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially fatal immune-related adverse event of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung cancer, and many machine-learning (ML), computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep-learning, and clinical models have been proposed to predict it. This systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and SinoMed, supplemented by citation searching and other sources, with independent dual-reviewer screening throughout and a reproducible PubMed verification search updated to August 16, 2026. Twelve peer-reviewed lung-cancer CIP-occurrence models (4,875 patients, 1,057 events) formed the main analysis; validation C-statistics were pooled on the logit scale with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp intervals, stratified by validation design. The pooled validation C-statistic was 0.82 (95% confidence interval 0.75-0.88) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 90.7%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 0.51-0.95, which is the decision-relevant quantity. By validation design, internal cross-validation pooled to 0.83, internal split-sample to 0.76, and only two studies reported external validation (0.84 and 0.92, described narratively). Imaging-based models (k = 8) showed numerically higher discrimination than clinical models (k = 4; 0.85 versus 0.78, moderator p = 0.46) without a statistically significant difference, and this comparison is confounded by design covariates. Estimates were stable on leave-one-out, alternative-model, cohort-overlap, and standard-error-source sensitivity analyses (range 0.80-0.84). Under the standard Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool, applied independently by two reviewers with consensus resolution, two studies were at high, nine at unclear, and one at low overall risk of bias; certainty of evidence was low (very low under a stricter appraisal scenario, which left the pooled estimate essentially unchanged). Current models separate risk groups on average but remain unready for clinical use; adequately powered, externally validated, and calibration-reported models are needed.

title: Vietnamese expert consensus on the diagnosis and multidisciplinary management of resectable non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Do QK, Pham DX, Nguyen HTT et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The management of resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved rapidly from a surgery-centered approach toward biomarker-informed, multimodality care integrating staging, pathology, surgery, perioperative systemic treatment, and postoperative surveillance. In Vietnam, implementation remains heterogeneous across institutions, particularly in access to fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT), invasive mediastinal staging, molecular testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. This project aimed to develop a Vietnamese multidisciplinary expert consensus to contextualize contemporary international evidence for clinical practice in Vietnam.
METHODS: A structured, modified Delphi-informed consensus process was conducted in Vietnam between August 2025 and January 2026. The workflow comprised seven stages: scoping; a baseline practice survey; initial draft development; expert review of parts 1 and 2; post-meeting written feedback, revision, electronic recirculation, and formal voting for these sections; a multidisciplinary consensus meeting and formal voting for parts 3 and 4; and editorial harmonization and consolidation. The panel included specialists in thoracic surgery, medical oncology, respiratory medicine, pathology, nuclear medicine, radiation oncology, and related disciplines. Classes of recommendation were adapted from the European Society of Cardiology framework. All statements submitted to formal consensus voting were formally rated, with consensus predefined as at least 75% agreement.
RESULTS: The final document comprised 35 consensus statements across four domains: preoperative diagnosis and staging (n=7), surgery and postoperative surveillance (n=8), neoadjuvant and perioperative treatment (n=12), and adjuvant treatment (n=8). Across the meeting rosters, 32 unique experts were identified, with strong representation from thoracic surgery and medical oncology. The baseline survey and expert discussions highlighted implementation gaps in FDG-PET/CT, invasive mediastinal staging, biomarker testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. All 35 consensus statements met the predefined threshold, with agreement ranging from 82% to 100%.
CONCLUSIONS: These consensus statements provide a multidisciplinary, evidence-informed framework for the diagnosis and management of resectable NSCLC across the perioperative pathway. By contextualizing international evidence within Vietnamese clinical practice, the document may help improve consistency of care, support biomarker-guided and multimodality treatment, and strengthen multidisciplinary decision-making across institutions.

title: Exploratory study to evaluate the combined effect of CBM588: Clostridium butyricum in platinum plus pemetrexed with pembrolizumab for non-small cell lung cancer-protocol of MIYABRO study.
authors: Tagawa R, Taniguchi H, Kaku N et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Platinum plus pemetrexed and pembrolizumab is a standard first-line treatment for advanced or recurrent non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable driver alterations, including tumors with a programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor proportion score (TPS) <50%. However, the clinical benefits vary, and biomarkers for this chemoimmunotherapy regimen remain limited. CBM588, a live biotherapeutic preparation containing Clostridium butyricum MIYAIRI, may modulate antitumor immunity by affecting the gut microbiota. The MIYABRO study aims to evaluate the additive efficacy and safety of CBM588 with platinum plus pemetrexed and pembrolizumab and to explore longitudinal gut microbiota dynamics.
METHODS: This is a multi-institutional, single-arm, phase II exploratory study enrolling 20 treatment-naïve patients with advanced or recurrent non-squamous NSCLC and a PD-L1 TPS <50%. Patients will receive continuous CBM588 from the start of the protocol treatment in combination with platinum, pemetrexed, and pembrolizumab. After four induction cycles, maintenance pemetrexed plus pembrolizumab will be continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoints are response rate and progression-free survival (PFS). Tumor response will be assessed according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Stool samples will be collected before treatment, cycle 3, and cycle 5 for 16S rRNA sequencing to evaluate microbial diversity and responder-associated taxa.
DISCUSSION: This trial will prospectively assess CBM588 added to platinum plus pemetrexed and pembrolizumab in NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS <50% while monitoring the gut microbiota. These findings may inform microbiota-targeted strategies for optimizing chemoimmunotherapy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (No. jRCT1071260004) on 6 April 2026.

title: Adjuvant alectinib versus crizotinib in completely resected ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer: a real-world retrospective cohort study.
authors: Yang Y, Liang S, Liu R et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following the phase III ALINA trial, adjuvant alectinib has become an important option for completely resected anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the adjuvant role of crizotinib remains uncertain, and real-world data directly comparing adjuvant alectinib with crizotinib are limited. We compared their efficacy, central nervous system (CNS) control, and safety in this setting.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 48 patients with R0-resected stage IA-IIIB ALK-positive NSCLC who underwent surgery between April 2012 and October 2023. Patients received alectinib 600 mg twice daily (n=26) or crizotinib 250 mg twice daily (n=22) after surgery. The primary endpoint was the 3-year disease-free survival (DFS) rate. Survival outcomes were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and unadjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using Cox regression. Safety was evaluated by treatment-related adverse events.
RESULTS: At a median follow-up of 84.6 months, alectinib was associated with longer DFS than crizotinib, with median DFS not reached versus 28.23 months, a 3-year DFS rate of 91.4% versus 41.4%, and an unadjusted HR of 0.20 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.08-0.47]. Brain metastasis-free survival (BMFS) also favored alectinib, with 3-year BMFS rates of 95.2% versus 74.8% and an HR of 0.16 (95% CI: 0.05-0.56). Most adverse events were grade 1-2; no grade ≥3 adverse events occurred with alectinib, compared with 27.3% with crizotinib.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of patients with completely resected ALK-positive NSCLC, adjuvant alectinib was associated with longer DFS, improved BMFS, and a more favorable safety profile than crizotinib. These findings are broadly consistent with the benefit of adjuvant alectinib observed in the phase III ALINA trial and support alectinib as the preferred adjuvant ALK-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) option over crizotinib. Further validation in larger multicenter real-world or prospective studies is warranted.

title: Considerations regarding a meta-analysis investigating the efficacy and safety of robotic-assisted thoracic surgery after neoadjuvant therapy in non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Jiao B, Wang L

title: Using Digital Outreach to Identify Individuals Eligible for Lung Cancer Screening: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Trial.
authors: Bundy R, Snavely AC, Miller DP et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer is the third most common cancer in the United States, but screening rates among high-risk adults remain low. In a multisite randomized trial conducted in two large academic health systems in North Carolina, we found that a digital health intervention delivered to patients at home increased lung screening (LCS) rates. While LCS reduces mortality, identifying and reaching eligible patients is challenging and limits screening uptake.
OBJECTIVE: This study examines the reach of a digital health outreach strategy for determining eligibility for LCS.
DESIGN: A secondary analysis of a pragmatic randomized trial.
PARTICIPANTS: Individuals aged 50 to 77 with a history of cigarette smoking received an invitation to use the digital health program at two academic health systems in North Carolina.
MAIN MEASURES: Reach of the engagement strategy overall and within demographic subgroups. Reach is defined by the proportion of patients completing LCS eligibility questions within 16 weeks of portal or text invitation.
KEY RESULTS: Of 26,909 individuals invited, 3,049 (11%) completed LCS eligibility questions within 16 weeks of invitation. Reach was higher among females, those aged 50-64, individuals with high/medium socioeconomic status, those with commercial insurance, and urban residents. White participants had higher reach compared to Black and Hispanic participants (12.8% vs 8.6% and 8.0%). Within 16 weeks of invitation, portal messages were read by 65.5% of recipients, with 17.1% visiting the mPATH-Lung landing page. Sending text invitations to those not reachable by portal expanded reach by 604 participants (from 2,445 to 3,409), compared to portal invitations alone.
CONCLUSIONS: This scalable outreach strategy engaged a large population for lung cancer screening. However, reach was found to be lower in historically underrepresented groups. Future strategies should continue leveraging multiple communication channels, including a cellphone text primary strategy, to maximize engagement and potentially improve equitable access to healthcare services.
